Top News
 
 
 
 
Dmitry Vinogradov/iStock Editorial via Getty Images
 
 
 Wall Street’s major indexes declined at least 1% each this week amid a deep technology trade rout, with some of the top semiconductor names shedding as much as 30%.

 Intel Corp. ( INTC ) dropped almost 26% this week, losing most of it on Friday, after a disappointing third-quarter earnings report that showed weaker-than-expected guidance due to manufacturing constraints tied to data centers. The stock had its worst day since the 1970s.

 Alphabet ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) also declined significantly this week, losing 12.2% after the technology giant reported weak Q3 results that were below consensus.

 Other tech giants that lost ground this week after posting Q3 earnings were Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Amazon ( AMZN ); among the top decliners were ServiceNow ( NOW ), Fortinet ( FTNT ), Guidewire Software ( GWRE ), Twilio ( TWLO ), and Salesforce ( CRM ), among others.

 Additionally, Anthropic ( ANTHRO ) filed for its IPO on Monday to be listed on the Nasdaq Global Exchange Market. The company reported revenue of $16.3B.

 Also in focus this week, the Federal Reserve announced its decision to maintain interest rates at the 3.75%-4.00% range on Wednesday, as widely expected. Communications by the Fed cited economic activity expanding at a strong pace. However, there were two dissents by Fed Gov. Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack.

 In other economic news, the Core PCE Price Index increased 0.3% month-over-month in September, in line with consensus estimates and unchanged from the rise in August, while the PCE Price Index, which includes food and energy, rose 0.5% month-over-month, as expected.

 Lastly, initial jobless claims unexpectedly slipped over the past week , and U.S. GDP grew more than estimated in Q3.

 For the week, the S&P ( SP500 ) lost -0.57% , while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( COMP:IND ) was -2% lower, and the blue-chip Dow ( DJI ) dropped -0.85% . Read a preview of next week's major events in Seeking Alpha's Catalyst Watch. 


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Global
 
 
 
 Spaceplane reveal 
 
 
 
Seeking Alpha
 
 
The Pentagon released an image of China's secretive spaceplane, shedding some light on Beijing's advancement in its space capabilities. Spaceplanes are reusable with enhanced maneuverability, making them more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites. While China said its reusable spacecraft tech is for "peaceful use," the Pentagon has flagged the risk of increased threats in the space domain. Read more.

Consumer Staples +1.6% . Utilities +2% . Financials +1.1% . Telecom -8.5% . Healthcare +3.1% . Industrials +1.7% . Information Technology -1.8% . Materials +2% . Energy +1% . Consumer Discretionary +1% . Real Estate +1.4% . 

 World Indices 
London +0.4% to 10,730. France +2.4% to 7,969. Germany +2.5% to 25,818. Japan +1% to 63,290. China -2.5% to 3,599. Hong Kong +0.9% to 23,294. India +1.8% to 74,460. 

 Commodities and Bonds 
Crude Oil WTI -0.3% to $102.95/bbl. Gold -3.1% to $3,884.9/oz. Natural Gas +9.2% to 2.883. Ten-Year Bond Yield -0.2 bps to 4.929. 

 Forex and Cryptos 
EUR/USD -0.38% . USD/JPY +0.45% . GBP/USD +0.11% . Bitcoin -4.4% . Litecoin -3.2% . Ethereum -4.9% . XRP -4% . 

 Top S&P 500 Gainers 
Pentair ( PNR ) +20% . Vertiv Holdings ( VRT ) +20% . Carvana ( CVNA ) +18% . Gen Digital ( GEN ) +17% . Global Payments ( GPN ) +17% . 

 Top S&P 500 Losers 
Reddit ( RDDT ) -36% . ServiceNow ( NOW ) -34% . F5 ( FFIV ) -26% . Fortinet ( FTNT ) -24% . Intel ( INTC ) -24% .
